questions.q: A pure tall pea plant TT is crossed with a short plant tt, and the F1 plants are selfed. What is the ratio of pure tall plants to short plants in F2?
questions.explanation: The parental cross TT x tt gives F1 plants that are all Tt and therefore tall because T is dominant. Selfing Tt x Tt gives genotypes TT, Tt, Tt, tt in the ratio 1:2:1. Comparing only pure tall TT with short tt gives the ratio 1:1.

questions.q: Round green peas RRyy are crossed with wrinkled yellow peas rrYY, giving F1 RrYy round yellow plants. After selfing F1, which pair represents the new phenotype combinations relative to the two parental combinations?
options: A) Round green and wrinkled yellow
B) Round yellow and wrinkled green
questions.answer: B) Round yellow and wrinkled green
questions.explanation: The parental phenotype combinations are round green and wrinkled yellow. Independent assortment in the F1 self-cross produces recombinations in F2 in addition to parental combinations. The new combinations are round yellow and wrinkled green, so option B is correct.

questions.q: In humans, a zygote receives an X chromosome from its father. What follows from the sex-chromosome mechanism described in the source?
options: A) The child must be male because the father supplied a sex chromosome
B) The sex cannot be inferred because the mother determines whether X or Y is supplied
C) The child develops as female because the mother supplies X and the father has supplied X
D) The child can be either male or female with equal probability even after the paternal X is known
questions.answer: C) The child develops as female because the mother supplies X and the father has supplied X
questions.explanation: Human females contribute an X chromosome through the egg. If the father also contributes X, the zygote is XX. Therefore the zygote develops as female, and this also shows why the paternal gamete determines whether the zygote is XX or XY.

questions.q: Which statement best distinguishes an acquired change from an inherited variation in the evolutionary context of the source?
options: A) Any decrease in body weight due to starvation is inherited by offspring
B) All changes that occur during life alter germ-cell DNA
C) Acquired traits always accumulate and directly form new species
D) A starvation-related decrease in body weight is acquired and is not, by itself, an inherited variation driving evolution
questions.answer: D) A starvation-related decrease in body weight is acquired and is not, by itself, an inherited variation driving evolution
questions.explanation: The source explicitly treats reduction in body weight due to starvation as a non-genetic change. Evolution depends on inherited variations that can pass across generations and alter gene frequencies. Therefore an acquired loss of weight does not itself become an inherited evolutionary change.
